newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ridley sees slightly better yr result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ridley sees slightly better yr result.

text.p: Stock feed manufacturer Ridley Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it expected the company's after tax earnings for the first half of the 1996/97 year would be in line with those of the first half of 1995/96.
Ridley chairman John Keniry told the annual meeting that the full year results were expected to come in slightly ahead of last year because of the recent rapid decline in grain prices.

Keniry said that Ridley expected another good result from its Canadian stock food supplier Feed-rite, with increases in both sales and profits. "For the first quarter Feed-Rite's earnings before interest and tax have exceeded by a comfortable margin both budget and last year," Keniry said.

Ridley's Cheetham Salt division was experiencing a continued slowing of demand in some sectors and earnings for the first quarter were in line with last year. "However, when the impact of the acquisition of 50 percent of Dominion Salt is taken into account we anticipate that overall earnings from our salt activities will be well ahead on last year," Keniry said.
First quarter earnings from Ridley's AgriProducts division had been below both budget forecast and last year's results, Keniry said.

Slow demand and margin pressures for feeds in New South Wales and Queensland and a significant cut in demand for supplements had offset buoyant stock feed sales in Victoria and South Australia, he said.
"All things considered we expect overall company after tax earnings to be in line with those of last year for the first half," Keniry said.

"When we look to the full year, we must recognise a very rapid decline in the past month or so in grain prices, and the somewhat unpredicatble impact on both us and our customers of these changes," Keniry said.
"Nevertheless on a full year basis, a cautious approach would be to say that we presently expect to come slightly ahead of last year," he said.
Ridley said last month it expected continued profit growth and was optimistic of achieving another record performance in the 1996/97 year to June 30.
Ridley reported a net profit of A$21.43 million in 1995/96.
At 11.40 a.m. (2340 GMT), Ridley shares were steady at A$1.69.
